travisLandUse100PercentDetermination.answer: NOT a Travis CAD ingest gap, and NOT the leaf-null defect this lane fixes. It is a STALE BAKE that predates a fix already merged.
evidence: Travis's conformant rows were baked 2026-08-30T02:36Z..05:27Z. The land-use resolution order (claim.propertyUseCode -> cad_property prop_id roll join -> owner-gated situs recovery) landed 2026-08-31, one day later; before it the ONLY source was claim.propertyUseCode, which Travis's conformant bodies carry null. That is written in the module's own header comment, whose worked examples are two Travis parcels.

cad_property for county_fips 48453 at tax_year 2026 holds 492,848 rows, of which 453,710 carry a non-null property_use_code. The data is present and joinable on prop_id; the bake simply never asked for it.

Cross-check that closes it: Caldwell was re-baked TODAY on current code and its post-bake land-use population is 48,586 - 16,862 = 31,724, which equals cad_property's coded-row count for 48055 at tax_year 2026 EXACTLY (31,724). The roll join is doing precisely what it claims, to the row.

Every one of Travis's 500,307 rows also carries NO provenance.landUseAbsence key at all -- that field did not exist when Travis was baked. So the 500,307 is not 500,307 earned absences; it is 500,307 unexamined nulls.

Any materially different result means the roll join does not reach Travis and should be raised, not absorbed.

perLeafRulings._principle: A leaf's cell state is earned WHERE THE ANSWER IS KNOWN. Two of these leaves are known at bake time and one is not, and that is the whole judgement.

baseFacts.landUse + provenance.landUseSo.state: absent-verified where the roll was consulted and missed; refused where it could not be consulted.
baseFacts.landUse + provenance.landUseSo.why: The bake ALREADY earns this verdict and already writes it -- at provenance.landUseAbsence, with authority, scopeSearched, an evaluation-time asOf and a per-parcel basis, guarded by assertLandUseAbsenceEarned. Measured on the two counties baked on current code, 16,862 of 16,862 Caldwell and 22,052 of 22,052 McLennan land-use absences are already verdict 'absent-verified'. Nothing new is being decided: the earned record is being PROMOTED from provenance to the leaf whose state it describes. The 09-05 join-miss ruling reaches this and landUseCode is its motivating case.
baseFacts.landUse + provenance.landUseSo.scopePrecision: fetchCountyLandUseRoll queries ONE declared tax year, not every tax year. The existing basis string already says so ('the Caldwell CAD roll at tax_year 2026 carries no coded row for prop_id join key X'), so the absence travels with its true scope. I am not widening that claim.
baseFacts.landUse + provenance.landUseSo.lookupFailedIsNotAbsentVerified: buildLandUseAbsence can also return 'lookup-failed' (gate-blocked county, no join key, roll never consulted). lookup-failed is not one of the four states. It maps to 'refused' -- a positive statement of non-determination -- and NEVER to absent-verified, carrying lookupVerdict:'lookup-failed' inside the wire so nothing is collapsed. Hays and Williamson are the gate-blocked counties and will exercise this branch on their next bake; Caldwell and McLennan produced zero lookup-faileds today.
baseFacts.landUse + provenance.landUseSo.walkHoleNoted: hauska-factory's classifyRequiredLeaf passes ANY non-empty object whose verdict is not one of the three absence verdicts as {state:'value', ok:true}. A wire carrying verdict 'lookup-failed' would therefore have PASSED, reading as a populated land use. Mapping to 'refused' is the honest state and is also the one that does not exploit that hole. The hole itself is hauska-factory's and is filed, not fixed here.
baseFacts.landUse + provenance.landUseSo.oneFixNotTwo: landUseSource mirrors baseFacts.landUse VERBATIM (same verdict, same basis, plus mirrors:'baseFacts.landUse'). Identical populations to the parcel in all six counties, as the dispatch said; mirroring rather than re-deciding is what makes them incapable of disagreeing.

baseFacts.situsCity + baseFacts.situsZip.why: The conformant claim IS the source for these two fields and it is ALWAYS read (it is the atom body the bake projects from) -- there is no join that can miss, so there is no lookup-failed branch. The authority owns the field the leaf is defined as: the leaf's own contract, written into the type, is 'situs ZIP as the source carries it', a postal fact that is never read as incorporation. absent-verified scoped to 'the cad-parcel-roll claim carries no situsCity for this parcel' is a verified absence of exactly that. It does NOT say the parcel has no city, and the basis is worded so it cannot be read that way.
baseFacts.situsCity + baseFacts.situsZip.basisDiversity: Basis names the parcel node id, so gradeAbsentVerifiedBasisDiversity cannot fire.

provenance.zoningSource.state: MIRROR of the served zoning rail, verbatim.
provenance.zoningSource.where: SERVE (structuralFactToFacetsWire.ts attachVerdictLayersToFacets), NOT the bake. This is the ruling the dispatch flagged as the one where a defensible-looking wrong answer is available, and it is not the answer the dispatch's own write-path pointer implies.
provenance.zoningSource.whyNotTheBake: The zoning rail's earned state does not exist at bake time and cannot be computed there. Read at source: the bake writes zoning:{district,...} when a stamp joined and zoning:null otherwise. The rail is decided at SERVE, in attachVerdictLayersToFacets, from two inputs the bake has no access to -- (1) the Factory's parcel_record_cell zoningDistrict rail via loadZoningFactForServe/zoningFactFromParcelRecord, which yields present, absent(absent-verified|not-applicable), or refused(code 'parcel-record-unaccounted'), and (2) the city-limits containment fact via zoningVerdictFromCityLimits, which yields not-applicable (unincorporated + declared unzoned doctrine), stamp-missing (inside an incorporated place, stamp absent, authority NOT absent) or unmeasured. A bake-side verdict would be this leaf inventing its own answer to a question the rail answers later with more information -- precisely the two-answers-that-can-disagree failure the dispatch forbids.
provenance.zoningSource.theDecisivePrecedent: facets.zoning is ITSELF baked as a bare null on 267,076 Travis rows and 486,218 Williamson rows, and it is a REQUIRED leaf, and it passes the walk. It passes because the serve attaches its four-state before the walk ever sees it. zoningSource is documented in the type as the 'top-level twin' of the zoning leaf's provenance. Twin and rail must be earned in the same place or they are not twins.
provenance.zoningSource.elginIsWhyMirroringMattersAndIsNotAnAbst: Elgin is deliberately absent from hauska-factory's DECLARED_COMPLETE (68.73% cell / 56.82% areal coverage), so its 1,706 unmatched parcels keep parcel_record's honest 'unaccounted', which LDT reads as state 'refused'. A bake-side absent-verified on those parcels is exactly the lie that passes every check and is already a standing ruling against. Mirroring cannot produce it: the mirror copies whatever the rail earned, so if the rail refuses, the twin refuses.
provenance.zoningSource.mirrorIsVerbatimNotTranslated: Same verdict string, same authority/scopeSearched/asOf/basis, plus mirrors:'zoning'. Deliberately NOT normalised into the four-state vocabulary: translating stamp-missing or unmeasured into 'refused' would make the twin say something the rail does not say, which is the disagreement this is meant to prevent. Identical content grades identically.
provenance.zoningSource.aRealCorrectnessBugThisAlsoCloses: Today, when parcel_record's zoning determination WINS over the baked stamp (attachVerdictLayersToFacets lines 104-111, an unconditional precedence added 2026-09-07), out.zoning is replaced but provenance.zoningSource still cites the OLD GIS layer URL. The served payload already contradicts its own rail on those parcels. The mirror fixes that too.
provenance.zoningSource.bakeSideChange: NONE. provenance.zoningSource stays exactly as it is in the bake -- the sourceUrl when a stamp joined, null otherwise -- because null is the honest bake-time statement and the serve is what earns the state, exactly as it already does for zoning itself.

Two copies of one fact get a divergence check, per DEV_PROCESS 2.4.

nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts: new assertRequiredLeafStatesEarned(payload) refusing (code REQUIRED_LEAF_BARE_NULL) any conformant payload where one of the four bake-owned leaves is a bare null. Called from the builder beside the existing two asserts, so a regression fails closed at the builder rather than at a walk three days later.

nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts: teach diffTier1KeyPaths that an old NULL leaf answered by a new EARNED ABSENCE at the same path is answered, not missing, and that the wire's own sub-leaves are not unexpected. Shape-based and narrow -- it cannot hide a genuinely dropped leaf, because the new payload must carry a well-formed wire at that exact path. DIVERGENCE_ALLOWLIST_NEW_SHAPE_PREFIXES is deliberately NOT widened, so its own exact-match test stays green.

structuralFactToFacetsWire.ts: attachVerdictLayersToFacets mirrors provenance.zoningSource onto whichever zoning cell it just decided -- the parcel_record provenance citation when parcel_record wins, the baked sourceUrl when the stamp stands, the absence wire verbatim otherwise.
